name: hunk
tagline: Review-first terminal diff viewer built for reading agent-authored changesets.
hook: An architecture guide to the shared review model, renderer boundaries, interface-specific tests, and three core project terms.
summary: Hunk has one central constraint: every interface shares the same review model, and renderers may not rebuild it themselves. The file also maps changes to test commands and defines three project terms.

techniques.title: The seam drawn as a pipeline
techniques.body: Two ASCII flows show how a diff becomes a review document and how an intent becomes a surface projection. Each stage names the module that owns it and the facts a renderer is to consume rather than recompute.
techniques.quote: Consume them; never re-derive those facts in a renderer.

techniques.title: Shrink-only baselines and append-only tombstones
techniques.body: The known-violations baseline may only shrink, while tombstone lists may only grow. Removing a violation requires deleting copies, adding a tombstone and adversarial fixture, registering consumers, and updating the audit.
techniques.quote: The known-violations baseline is shrink-only: fix an edge, rerun `bun run deps:baseline`, and never add to it.

techniques.title: Checks selected by kind of change
techniques.body: Rendering changes need type, integration, TTY, and real-terminal checks. Interaction work needs PTY coverage; broker work needs the Node adapter suite. The guide also names four suites excluded by default.
techniques.quote:
`bun run test` does not include review conformance, PTY, TTY smoke, or real-Node adapter
conformance

techniques.title: A stated voice for comments
techniques.body: Header comments are written in active voice and lead with what the module does. Two phrasings are named as the ones to avoid, both of which describe the architecture's opinion of itself rather than its behavior.
techniques.quote:
Avoid passive or self-important framing ("The one place where…", "the single
  source of truth for…") — name the behavior, not the architecture's opinion of itself.

techniques.title: Three words defined
techniques.body: layout for structural arrangement, geometry for aggregate spatial data, bounds for one concrete visible extent. Three definitions that settle naming for everything in that area.

techniques.title: Generated files named with their generators
techniques.body: Four generated outputs list their source and rebuild command. Updating a session fixture also requires a protocol version bump and deletion of the previous fixture.

steal: If several surfaces share semantics, draw the pipeline and name the owner of each stage.
Give every known-violations baseline a stated direction of travel, and enforce it in CI.
If your default test command excludes suites, say which ones. Agents run the obvious command.
Define the three or four words your domain keeps arguing about.
